summary: Master NGO conflict mediation and team resolution strategies. Learn TKI frameworks and Interest-Based Relational methods for field teams. Enroll today.
lede: Conflict Management and Mediation in NGO Teams gives professionals a structured way to address workplace disputes before they disrupt projects or humanitarian and development outcomes. You will practice conflict audits, stakeholder-interest mapping, Nonviolent Communication techniques, and neutral mediation for high-pressure team situations. The course also covers BATNA-based negotiation, restorative justice circles, grievance-handling templates, and conflict resolution across distributed teams using virtual collaboration platforms. You will develop a practical toolkit and learn to use team-health KPIs to report progress to leadership and donors with data-driven insights.
audienceIntro: This program is essential for professionals responsible for team performance and operational stability in the non-profit and humanitarian sectors.
modules: Foundations of NGO Team Conflict Dynamics
Cross-Cultural Communication and Field Team Cohesion
Power Dynamics and Intersectional Conflict Analysis
Digital Conflict Management in Distributed NGO Teams
De-escalation and Safety in High-Stakes Environments
prerequisites: Participants should have at least 2-3 years of experience in a supervisory or project management role within an NGO or humanitarian organization. Familiarity with basic team management concepts is required. Pre-reading on the Core Humanitarian Standard (CHS) is recommended but not mandatory.
